title: Coding Challenge 6: WebSocket Connection
description:
Learn how to establish real-time, bidirectional communication using the native browser WebSocket API. Unlike HTTP requests which follow a single request-response cycle and close, a WebSocket creates a persistent connection where client and server can send messages to each other at any time.

In this challenge, you will connect to the public WebSocket echo service ('wss://echo.websocket.org'). The echo server reflects back any text message it receives.

You will build a 'WebSocketClient' class and a 'sendEchoMessage' helper function:
1. WebSocketClient class:
   - constructor(url = 'wss://echo.websocket.org'): Stores this.url and initializes this.socket = null
   - connect(): Creates this.socket = new WebSocket(this.url) and returns a Promise that resolves when connection is opened ('open' event) and rejects on 'error'
   - send(message): Sends the message string via this.socket.send(message)
   - onMessage(callback): Listens for incoming 'message' events and passes event.data to the callback
   - close(): Closes the connection using this.socket.close()
2. sendEchoMessage(message, url): An async function that connects, sends a message, waits for the echoed response, closes the connection, and returns the echoed string.
requirements: Create a 'WebSocketClient' class with constructor accepting 'url' (defaults to 'wss://echo.websocket.org')
'connect()' must create 'this.socket = new WebSocket(this.url)' and return a Promise resolving when connection is open
'onMessage(callback)' must listen for incoming messages and invoke 'callback(event.data)'
Implement 'sendEchoMessage(message, url)' to connect, send a message, wait for echo, close connection, and return the echoed string
hints: In connect(), return 'new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ... })'. Inside, attach listeners for 'open' (to resolve) and 'error' (to reject)
In onMessage(callback), listen with 'this.socket.addEventListener("message", e => callback(e.data))' or 'this.socket.onmessage = e => callback(e.data)'
In sendEchoMessage, you can instantiate your WebSocketClient, await client.connect(), send the message, wait for the echo in onMessage, close, and resolve with the received text

tests.name: WebSocketClient class exists with constructor
tests.test: function() { try { if (typeof WebSocketClient !== 'function') { return { success: false, message: 'WebSocketClient class does not exist' }; } const client = new WebSocketClient(); if (typeof client !== 'object' || client.url !== 'wss://echo.websocket.org') { return { success: false, message: 'WebSocketClient should set default url to "wss://echo.websocket.org"' }; } const custom = new WebSocketClient('wss://custom.url'); if (custom.url !== 'wss://custom.url') { return { success: false, message: 'WebSocketClient should accept custom url parameter' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: WebSocketClient has required methods
tests.test: function() { try { const client = new WebSocketClient(); const methods = ['connect', 'send', 'onMessage', 'close']; for (const m of methods) { if (typeof client[m] !== 'function') { return { success: false, message: 'Missing method: ' + m + '()' }; } } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: All required methods (connect, send, onMessage, close) exist ✓

tests.name: connect() opens WebSocket connection and resolves
tests.test: async function() { let client = null; try { client = new WebSocketClient(); const connPromise = client.connect(); if (!connPromise || typeof connPromise.then !== 'function') { return { success: false, message: 'connect() must return a Promise' }; } await connPromise; if (!client.socket) { return { success: false, message: 'client.socket was not initialized' }; } if (client.socket.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) { return { success: false, message: 'WebSocket readyState should be OPEN (1), got ' + client.socket.readyState }; } client.close(); return { success: true }; } catch(e) { if (client) try { client.close(); } catch(_) {} return { success: false, message: 'connect() failed: ' + e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: connect() successfully opened connection to echo server ✓

tests.name: send() and onMessage() receive echoed message
tests.test: async function() { let client = null; try { client = new WebSocketClient(); await client.connect(); const testMsg = 'Hello WebSocket ' + Date.now(); const received = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Timed out waiting for message echo')), 5000); client.onMessage(data => { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(data); }); client.send(testMsg); }); client.close(); if (received !== testMsg) { return { success: false, message: 'Expected echoed message "' + testMsg + '", got: "' + received + '"' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { if (client) try { client.close(); } catch(_) {} return { success: false, message: 'Echo test failed: ' + e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: Successfully sent and received echoed message over WebSocket ✓

tests.name: close() terminates the connection
tests.test: async function() { let client = null; try { client = new WebSocketClient(); await client.connect(); client.close(); const state = client.socket.readyState; if (state !== WebSocket.CLOSING && state !== WebSocket.CLOSED) { return { success: false, message: 'Expected socket to be CLOSING (2) or CLOSED (3), got readyState ' + state }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: close() cleanly closes the WebSocket connection ✓

tests.name: sendEchoMessage() sends and returns echoed text
tests.test: async function() { try { if (typeof sendEchoMessage !== 'function') { return { success: false, message: 'sendEchoMessage function does not exist' }; } const testMsg = 'CodingChallenge-Echo-' + Math.floor(Math.random() * 10000); const echoResult = await sendEchoMessage(testMsg); if (echoResult !== testMsg) { return { success: false, message: 'Expected echo to return "' + testMsg + '", got: "' + echoResult + '"' }; } return { success: true }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: 'sendEchoMessage failed: ' + e.message }; } }
tests.successMessage: sendEchoMessage() successfully connects, echoes, and returns the message ✓
